title: WPMS/1188/2016 of Pran Nath Vs Sushila Devi AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPMS No. 1188 of 2016
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Neeraj Garg, Advocate for the
respondents.
The petitioner had preferred a
substitution application before the learned
Appellate Court seeking substitution of the
heirs of the sole respondent. The objection was
raised by the respondent to the Appeal before
the Court below to the effect that one of the
proposed heirs is not the heir of the deceased
respondent and, further more, that one of the
proposed heirs is a minor, who is not
represented by the natural guardian, and also
that the substitution has been preferred without
an application for setting aside abatement,
hence, was not tenable.
While considering the objection, the
Court has passed the impugned order dated
29.02.2016, directing the petitioner to make the
necessary amendment in the substitution
application its this order, which is impugned in
the writ petition.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that the proposed heirs of the
respondent, as he has submitted in the
substitution application, are the actual heirs,
which he intends to be substituted in place of
deceased respondent no. 1 of the Appeal.
Hence, there is no necessity for the Sixth
Additional District Judge, to issue any such
direction to the petitioner to file an amendment
application. That means to say that the
petitioner does not intend to amend the
substitution application in light of the objection
as taken by the respondent before the Court
below.

It has been argued by the learned counsel
for the petitioner that wherever such a
controversy arises pertaining to the issue as to
who would be the actual heir required to be
substituted on the death of the party to the
proceedings all the question in relation thereto
are to be decided by the Court below itself in
view of the provisions contained under Order
22 Rule 5.
Hence, the objection pertaining to the
minority of the proposed defendant or the
question pertaining to the one of the proposed
heir not being the heir are the questions, which
are to be decided by the Appellate Court under
Order 22 Rule 5. However, this will not include
a right to adjudicate upon the application or
issue pertaining to Order 22 Rule 9.
Subject to the above observation, the writ
petition stands disposed of with a direction to
the learned Appellate Court to decide the
substitution application as preferred by the
petitioner in the light of the provisions
contained under Order 22 Rule 5.
However, there would be no order as to
cost.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 26.06.2019
Pooja
